claims.quote: a regression in the "create a new stack when the original error has no stack" path, for example if the fallback were removed, would no longer be caught by this test

known_problems.reason: Says what goes wrong: a regression in the no-stack fallback path 'would no longer be caught by this test', and the assertions 'pass either way'. Identifies the cause as a fault: the input changed to `new Error('original')`, 'which always has a `stack` string', so the test 'takes the first branch, which is the opposite of what the test name says'.

claims.notes: The comment names the changed test 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' and says it now passes a real Error, so GraphQLError copies its stack and the fallback branch is never run; a regression in the fallback would go unnoticed. That is GT-k1's consequence and cause. A scratch run of the pinned GraphQLError showed new Error('original').stack is a truthy string and e.stack === original.stack with the post-PR body, i.e. the copy branch runs. The mocha run of the test file passes (13 passing). The known problem settles questions 2 to 4.
